newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Tight allocations support Minas.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Tight allocations support Minas.

text.p: Asia's heavy crude market stayed well supported by Japanese demand on Wednesday, traders said.
Minas was likely to be further supported after Indonesia announced on Wednesday that it had lowered export allocations for August compared with July.
Indonesia allocated just 38,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of Minas for August, from 52,000 bpd in July.
Traders said the cut in the Minas volume was due to preparations for the start-up of the new 65,000-bpd crude distillation unit at the Balikpapan refinery in August.

Traders said they expected Japanese demand to remain strong but widespread talk since last week that a Japanese refiner had bought a parcel of August Minas from an equity producer at ICP +85/+90 cents per barrel were denied.
Traders said it was fair to value the Minas premium for August around ICP +80/+85, but no trade had actually taken place at that level.
The light crude market was thin, with Belida premiums still talked at low levels of around ICP +15/+20, although the August allocations of 16,000 bpd was almost half that of July.
Traders said there was adequate light crudes in August.
Belida normally trades at a premium of +40/+50 cents.
August trading for the Middle East crudes was almost finished, except for two cargoes of Masila held by a western trader and a European major.
A European major sold its last two cargoes of Murban on Tuesday, at Dubai +78 cents per barrel to Thailand, and at Dubai +73.5 cents to a Japanese refiner.
Another European major was heard to have rolled its remaining August parcels of Abu Dhabi into September.
